title: Sections for pages
summary: Whole page sections (heroes, pricing, FAQs, sign-in) built from the same tokens, so a page can be assembled in minutes and still look designed.

components.name: Hero, split
components.summary: Headline, one sentence and one action beside one picture. data-variant composes the first screen four more ways: overlap, edge, product and bleed.
called: top section of a landing page with a screenshot
first screen of a SaaS site

anatomy.name: Headline
anatomy.text: What it does, under 12 words.

anatomy.name: Primary action
anatomy.text: One filled button; the second is ghost.

anatomy.name: Product
anatomy.text: The real product, not stock art.

components.prompt: Build a split hero: left column with a short eyebrow, a headline under 12 words, a one-sentence lede, one primary button and at most one quiet link; right column shows the product in a framed card. Stack on narrow containers. Tokens only.
components.debug: Debug my hero. Rule out: two primary buttons; a headline over two lines on desktop; illustration instead of product; text over a busy image with low contrast. The symptom:
components.note: The plain split is the kit's habit: give the first screen a composition that fits the subject. data-variant="overlap" (the picture runs off the end edge, the words on a block of the page ground over its edge), "edge" (a quiet split, the picture full height to the screen's edge), "product" (the device or object first and large, the words beneath), "bleed" (a photograph across the screen, the words on its calm side: data-calm="start|end|bottom" and data-tone="dark" for light words, with a scrim only under them). The visual slot holds a photograph, an art panel (or scene) or a device frame. Keep data-part="frame" for the plain split with a live product mock. The reassurance note under the buttons is opt-in.

components.name: Hero, centred
components.summary: A centred headline with an announcement pill, two actions and a framed product shot below. data-variant="wide" sets a larger statement over a picture that runs from edge to edge.
aliases: centred statement over a wide photo

anatomy.name: Announcement

anatomy.name: Headline

components.prompt: Build a centred hero: an announcement pill ("New" chip + text + arrow) linking to the changelog, a headline capped at 16ch, a lede, a primary and a secondary button, then a framed product shot. Keep text centred only because every line is short.
components.debug: Debug my centred hero. Rule out: centred paragraphs longer than three lines; a pill nobody can click; the product shot cropped on mobile; gradient headline text. The symptom:
components.note: data-variant="wide": no pill, a headline up to 92px, one sentence, one action and one quiet link, then <div data-part="visual"> with a photograph, an art panel or a device running edge to edge (21:9, 16:9 on tablets, 4:3 on phones), closing the section.

components.name: Stats band

called: row of big numbers on a landing page

anatomy.name: Figure
anatomy.text: Large display type, tabular figures, units written out. Counts once; the HTML holds the real value.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.text: Says what the number counts and over what period.

anatomy.text: Hairlines group the figures; no cards.

components.prompt: Build a stats band: a small eyebrow heading, then a <dl> of four figures in a row (two by two when narrow), each a large display-type value in tabular figures above a plain label that says what was counted and over what period, divided by hairlines, no boxes or icons. Mark each value data-count: it counts up to the number written in it once, when half on screen (1.4s, ease-out), keeping its width; data-count-from starts it higher (99 for 99.98%). Without script, under reduced motion and in print the real number simply shows.
components.debug: Debug my stats band. Rule out: rounded vanity numbers with no period ("10k+ users"); icons on every figure; numbers that jump width when counting up; boxes around each stat. The symptom:

about the person (this happens by itself). No photographs, or the people are speakers, partners or a studio: data-variant="list" sets them as ruled rows of name, role and one line, with no grey tiles. Put an in place of the initials when there are photographs: same ratio for everyone.

components.name: Before and after
components.summary: One picture in two states with a divider you drag across it. A native range input under the hood: arrow keys, pointer, a tap anywhere and touch all work.
components.pattern: input type=range over two clipped layers
called: the slider you drag to see before and after
compare two versions of the same picture

anatomy.name: Before
anatomy.text: The whole picture in its old state; shows left of the divider.

anatomy.name: After
anatomy.text: The same picture, new; shows right of the divider.

anatomy.name: Divider
anatomy.text: A line the full height with a 44px knob. Rings when the slider has keyboard focus.

components.prompt: Build a before-and-after section: a centred heading and one line, then a 16:9 frame (4:5 on phones, radius xl) holding two full-size layers, before and after, each role="img" with an aria-label. The after layer is clipped with clip-path: inset(0 0 0 var(--pos)). A native <input type="range"> covers the frame with opacity 0, so arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Home and End, pointer drag, a tap anywhere and touch all move it; it sets --pos and an aria-valuetext like "60% before, 40% after". A divider line with a 44px round knob sits at --pos and shows the focus ring while the input has keyboard focus; labels in the top corners fade when the divider reaches them. touch-action: pan-y so the page still scrolls on phones. Captions for both sides under the frame.
components.debug: Debug my before-and-after slider. Rule out: a custom div with pointer events only (no keyboard, no screen reader); two pictures of different sizes or crops; the page unable to scroll on a phone over the slider (touch-action); the focus ring missing because the input is invisible; labels covering the divider. The symptom:
components.note: Two pictures of the same thing at the same size: a room before and after, a document before and after, a photograph before and after retouching. Passing two lists of strings to the React component still gives the older two-column layout.

components.name: Sticky story (pinned scene)
components.summary: The picture stays pinned while three or four steps scroll past beside it, and it changes with each step: it cross-fades to that step's state, settles in, and the part the step is about is ringed.
aliases: picture that changes as you scroll
called: the section where the picture stays and the text scrolls
steps that change the screenshot as you scroll
the product stays still while the steps go by

anatomy.name: Step text
anatomy.text: A short heading and one line. The step at the middle of the screen is in full ink; the others step back.

anatomy.name: Pinned picture
anatomy.text: One per step, all in one pinned cell: the same frame in that step's state. They cross-fade as the steps pass.

anatomy.name: Marked part
anatomy.text: The part a step is about gets a ring that draws in as the step arrives.

components.prompt: Build a pinned scroll scene: a large heading, then an ordered list of three or four steps in a two-column grid. Each <li> is display: contents and holds its text (a heading and one line) and its own picture (data-part="visual"): the same product frame in that step's state. Texts stack in the left column, each 60svh tall; every picture sits in one right-hand cell spanning all rows, position: sticky, vertically centred, on a tinted panel. Each step's text is a named view-timeline shared with its picture through timeline-scope on the <li>; the picture fades and settles from scale 0.965 while the text is within half a step of the screen's middle, and any element with data-mark inside it gets an accent ring that draws in a moment later. Without scroll-driven animation support an IntersectionObserver on a line at the middle of the screen marks the step data-active instead. Under reduced motion or without script each step is a still row, text beside its picture; under 760px each picture sits under its own text and nothing is pinned. Inside a preview box with nothing to scroll the steps take turns on a timer. Transform and opacity only.
components.debug: Debug my pinned scene. Rule out: an ancestor with overflow hidden or auto (sticky stops working); the text steps shorter than 60svh (the fade timing assumes it); pictures that are different frames rather than one frame in different states; more than four steps; a second pinned moment on the same page; inactive text dimmed under reduced motion. The symptom:
code: li { display: contents; timeline-scope: --step } [data-part=text] { view-timeline: --step block }
components.note: One per page, and it counts as one of the page's two scroll moments. Three or four steps with one frame (a phone, a browser, a photograph) in each step's state: the screen changes, the frame does not. Put data-mark on what the step is about.

components.prompt: Build an offers section for a shop, a maker or a place: a heading, then two to four cards in a row (two across under 860px, one under 560px). components.prompt: Build a visit section for a place: on the left the full postal address in an <address> at a larger size, a "Getting here" list with one line per way of arriving (on foot, by bike, by car, by train) each with a real time or number, and phone and email as links (tel: and mailto:). On the right an opening hours table that lists all seven days with closed days written as "Closed", marks today in bold, and a line above it that says in words "Open now, until 18:00", "Opens today at 9:00" or "Closed now". Add one line for exceptions (holidays, last orders). No embedded map image; if a map matters, link to one.
components.debug: Debug my location and hours section. Rule out: hours as an image or a paragraph; days missing because they are closed; "open now" shown only by a green dot; a phone number that is not a tel: link; a map embed that loads a megabyte of script; times in a format locals do not use. The symptom:

components.name: Hero, statement
components.summary: A type-led hero: one very large headline across the page, then a ruled row with the pitch, the action and three facts. data-variant="tucked" tucks a small picture into the headline; "poster" sets a date enormous as the composition.
called: hero with just a huge headline
big text at the top and no picture
the opening line that fills the screen

anatomy.name: Headline
anatomy.text: The picture. Up to 100px, set tight, 15 characters a line, balanced.

anatomy.name: Ruled row
anatomy.text: A strong rule, then the pitch and action left, facts right.

anatomy.name: Three facts
anatomy.text: True figures with their unit and what they count.

components.note:
Use this hero when there is no picture worth showing, or when the words are the product (a studio, a publication, a venue, a brand, a manifesto). The headline must be a real claim of six to ten words; it carries the whole first screen. data-variant="tucked": put
(a photograph, art panel or phone) before the

; it floats on the end side and the lines run round it. data-variant="poster": add

14–15May 2027

before the h1; the date is set huge, an optional picture sits on the end side; put it on the brand band (data-tone="accent").
components.prompt: Build a statement hero: a small eyebrow, then an <h1> set very large (clamp from 44px to 100px with the container width), tight line height (0.98), tight tracking, 15 characters a line, text-wrap: balance. Under it a row that starts with a strong hairline: on the left the lede at 20px in secondary ink (44 characters a line) and the actions (one primary, one ghost); on the right a <dl> of three facts, each a large tabular figure over a plain label, divided by hairlines. Under 820px the row stacks; under 480px the facts become rows. No image, no background effect behind the headline: the type is the picture.
components.debug: Debug my type-led hero. Rule out: a headline that is a slogan with no claim; more than ten words at this size; lines broken mid-phrase (balance, or break by hand); a gradient or image behind the type; facts with no unit or period; three buttons. The symptom:

components.name: Hero with video
components.summary: A headline and one action above a wide picture that is a still first and becomes a muted, looping film when motion is allowed, with a pause button always on it.
components.pattern: <video muted loop playsinline> over a poster
called: the top section with a video playing
hero with a muted background film

anatomy.name: Headline
anatomy.text: What and where, under ten words, on the left edge.

anatomy.name: Action
anatomy.text: One primary action beside the lede.

anatomy.name: Still
anatomy.text: Shown first and whenever the film is not playing: an , or an art panel until there is one.

anatomy.name: Film
anatomy.text: Fetched and played only when motion is allowed and Save-Data is off; fades in once it plays, so nothing shifts.

components.prompt: Build a hero with video: a large headline on the left with the lede and one primary button in a column to its right, then a wide media box (16:9; 2:1 on wide screens; 4:5 on phones) with a radius. Inside it a still (an or a placeholder panel) fills the box; over it a
components.debug: Debug my video hero. Rule out: autoplay under reduced motion or Save-Data; no pause button (WCAG 2.2.2); sound on; the box resizing when the film loads (give it an aspect-ratio); the file downloading for people who never see it (preload="none" plus data-src); the headline set over the moving film. The symptom:
code: <video data-part="video" muted loop playsinline preload="none"><source data-src="film.mp4">
components.note: Only with a real film of the subject (a place, a product in use), 8 to 20 seconds, muted, under 4 MB. Put its path in data-src and a still from it in the poster. Without one, keep the still: it is the same hero. data-variant="full" (with data-tone="dark"): the film or its still is the whole first screen and the words sit at its foot over a scrim; the pause button moves to the top corner.

components.name: Hero, board
components.summary: A first screen whose picture is the subject's own board: a café's menu with prices, or departures with times, set large on a dark board beside the headline and one action.
states: with a picture behind the board
called: hero with the menu and prices as the main picture
a departures board at the top of a transport site
first screen that shows today's times
café home page with the prices up front

anatomy.name: Headline
anatomy.text: What it is and where, under ten words.

anatomy.name: Board
anatomy.text: The subject's own board on the palette's dark ground: it is the picture.

anatomy.name: First row
anatomy.text: The next sailing or today's coffee, a size larger; every figure in one column.

components.prompt: Build a board hero: on the start side an h1 (under ten words), one sentence and one primary button; on the end side, as the picture, a <figure> on a dark ground holding the subject's board: a caption row (the board's name and one note) over a strong rule, then an <ol> whose rows share one grid (subgrid) so every price or time lines up: a menu has the name with a one-line note under it and the price on the end side in tabular figures; departures have the time in the mono face, the place, the stop and a status. The first row is a size larger. Under 900px the board goes under the words. With an optional picture, the picture sits on the end side and the board rises over its foot.
components.debug: Debug my board hero. Rule out: prices or times that do not line up (use one grid for every row); a chalk texture or a handwriting face; more than six rows; the board's rows counted as the hero's paragraph (keep them in the <figure>); a status shown by colour alone. The symptom:
components.note: For a café, bar, bakery or restaurant with four to six priced things (menu), or a ferry, bus, train or shuttle with times (departures). The rows are real prices and times from the brief; never invent them.

components.name: Hero, cover
components.summary: The first screen set like a magazine cover: the name as a masthead across the column, a date line between two rules, one large picture and the cover line with one action.
called: the name huge across the top like a magazine
portfolio hero with my name big
journal or newsletter home page header

anatomy.name: Masthead
anatomy.text: The name, sized from its length to fill the column.

anatomy.name: Date line
anatomy.text: Two or three facts between two rules: what, where, when.

anatomy.name: Cover line
anatomy.text: The claim in one sentence, set as display type beside the picture's foot.

components.prompt: Build a cover hero: an h1 masthead with the name set as large as the column allows (font-size from its length: 100cqi divided by characters × 0.62, capped at 15rem; line-height 0.88; tight tracking), then a date line of two or three short facts spread across the column between two strong rules, then a 12-column grid: one large picture (3:2) over eight columns and, on the last four, the cover line (one sentence in the display face, about 32px) with one primary action at the picture's foot. Stack under 760px.
components.debug: Debug my cover hero. Rule out: a masthead that runs out of the column (set --cover-len); a second headline competing with it; rules on every section below (the cover's two rules are its own); more than one picture. The symptom:
components.note: For a publication, a studio, a portfolio, a person or a named festival: something whose name is worth setting big. The date line is real: a place, a year, an issue.

components.name: Hero, mosaic
components.summary: Three to five pictures set as one interlocking composition, with the headline in the corner they leave free.
components.pattern: <section> + <ul> of pictures on a shared grid
called: hero with a collage of photos
top of a shop page with several product shots
first screen with three or four pictures and the headline in a corner

anatomy.name: Large picture
anatomy.text: The strongest picture.

anatomy.name: Tall picture
anatomy.text: The one that reads as a portrait.

anatomy.name: Words
anatomy.text: The headline, one sentence and one action in the corner the pictures leave.

components.prompt: Build a mosaic hero: a 12-column, six-row grid (rows about a tenth of the screen's height). A list of three to five pictures shares the grid through subgrid: the first over six columns and three rows, the second three columns and five rows tall, the third three columns stepping down a row, a fourth under the second, a fifth in the top corner. The headline, one sentence and one action sit in the six columns and three rows left free at the bottom start. Pictures share one radius and one tone. Under 860px the words go first and the pictures run two across, the first one wide.
components.debug: Debug my mosaic hero. Rule out: pictures of different tones or subjects; more than five; the headline over a picture; tiles of the same size (that is a grid, not a mosaic); a stock photograph among them. The symptom:
components.note: Only with three or more real pictures of the subject (or one drawing each until they exist). With one strong photograph, use hero-split data-variant="bleed" instead.

components.name: Service list
components.summary: Things on offer as ruled rows: a name, one sentence, how long it takes and the price, each in its own column down the list. Also a programme with times, or a menu.
called: a list of services with prices instead of cards
a restaurant menu with prices lined up

anatomy.name: Name
anatomy.text: The plain name of the service or session. A row that links somewhere is one <a>.

anatomy.name: One sentence
anatomy.text: What happens, or who is speaking. Never longer than two lines at full width.

anatomy.name: Time or place
anatomy.text: How long it takes, which room, which days. One short phrase in its own column.

anatomy.name: Price
anatomy.text: In full, right-aligned, tabular. Leave the column out when nothing has a price.

components.prompt: Build a list of services as ruled rows, not cards: a heading, then a <ul> where every row shares one grid (use subgrid) so the names, the one-sentence descriptions, the durations and the prices each line up in a column down the list. A strong rule above the first row and a hairline under each. A row that leads somewhere is a single link with an arrow at the end that moves 3px on hover; a row that does not is plain. Prices are right-aligned with tabular figures. An optional leading column holds a start time in mono for a programme, and a small mono label can sit above each list when there are several (days, courses). Under 760px the name and price share the first line and the sentence and duration go beneath. A note under the list says when the prices apply from.
components.debug: Debug my service or price list. Rule out: prices that do not line up down the list; rows of different structure; "Contact us" in place of every price; cards where rows would scan faster; a description longer than two lines; times in mixed formats; links that all say "Learn more". The symptom:
components.note:
Use this instead of cards when there are four or more things, or when people compare prices and times. A row is the
  • itself, or one or
    inside it (use when the row leads somewhere). Columns you do not use (when, meta, price) collapse. For a programme, put first in each row and a

    above each day's

      . It needs the full width: do not put it beside a rail.

components.name: Scroll statement
components.summary: One large sentence that lights up word by word as it scrolls past. The keynote beat: a claim set big, with its quieter half in secondary ink.
called: text that lights up as you scroll

anatomy.name: The claim
anatomy.text: Twelve to twenty-five words. Each word brightens in turn as the section crosses the screen.

anatomy.name: The quiet half
anatomy.text: The second half in secondary ink: hierarchy without more words.

anatomy.name: Proof line
anatomy.text: Two or three facts in mono that back the claim.

components.prompt: Build a statement section: one sentence of 12 to 25 words set very large (about 4.5rem at desktop, tight tracking, line-height 1.06, max 22ch), with its second half in secondary ink. Under it a short mono line of facts. As the section scrolls through the screen each word goes from 16% to full opacity in turn, using a named view-timeline on the section and an animation-range per word set by a small script that wraps the words in spans. Without support, without the script and under reduced motion the sentence is simply at full strength.
components.debug: Debug my scroll statement. Rule out: a paragraph instead of one sentence; words hidden when scroll-driven animations are not supported; text dimmed under reduced motion; more than one of these on a page; the sentence repeating the headline above it. The symptom:
components.note: One per page at most, between two busy sections: it is a pause, not a section of content. 12 to 25 words, a claim someone could disagree with, with facts in the note line. Never a paragraph.

components.name: Stack cards
components.summary: Steps as large cards that pin near the top and stack as you scroll, each with a number, a title, one line and a picture. Replaces a numbered list of paragraphs.
called: cards that stack on top of each other as you scroll
how it works with a picture per step

anatomy.name: Number
anatomy.text: In mono, at the top of the card.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.text: Three to six words, large.

anatomy.name: One line
anatomy.text: Twenty words at most.

anatomy.name: Picture
anatomy.text: A device frame, an invoice sheet, a chart, a photograph, or one figure set large.

components.prompt: Build a steps section as stacking cards: each step is a large card (min-height about 380px, radius xl, hairline border) split into text on the left (a mono number at the top, a large title near the bottom, one line under it) and a picture on the right. Each <li> is position: sticky with top: calc(84px + index * 16px), so as you scroll each card slides over the last and the edges of the earlier cards stay visible above it. Alternate the card surface. Under 720px and under reduced motion they are a plain list with the picture under the text.
components.debug: Debug my stacking cards. Rule out: an ancestor with overflow hidden (it breaks sticky); cards of different heights; paragraphs instead of one line; no picture, so the stack is three boxes of text; more than five cards. The symptom:
components.note: Three to five steps, each with a real picture: the screen it happens on, the document it produces, or one figure. Never an ancestor with overflow: hidden. One stack per page.

components.name: Media band
components.summary: One claim and one large picture on a dark ground, with three facts under it. The cinematic beat of a page; the picture settles into place as it scrolls in.
called: a dark section with one big product picture
a break from all the white sections

anatomy.name: Claim
anatomy.text: Three to eight words, centred, with a quiet second half.

anatomy.name: Picture
anatomy.text: The product's real screen, a chart, a photograph or an art panel, large, with a glow behind it.

anatomy.name: Three facts
anatomy.text: Large figures with a label each.

components.prompt: Build a media band: a full-width section on a dark ground (the palette's own dark tokens on this section only) with generous padding. A centred claim of three to eight words, very large, its second half in secondary ink. Under it one large picture (max 1040px) with a soft radial glow of the accent behind it; it scales from 0.9 to 1 as it scrolls in. A one-line caption, then three facts in a row, large figures with small labels, divided by hairlines.
components.debug: Debug my media band. Rule out: more than one dark band on the page; a paragraph instead of a claim; a small picture lost in the dark; the glow behind text; text colours that do not follow the dark tokens. The symptom:
components.note: At most one dark band per page, from the middle on, for the strongest picture you have. Any block takes data-tone="dark" the same way. data-variant="bleed": the picture runs from one edge of the screen to the other (21:9, 4:3 on phones), square-cornered and without the glow; for a photograph or a drawing as wide as the page.

components.name: Product reveal
components.summary: The product rises from lying back, like a lid opening, and settles flat and full size as it reaches the screen. One scroll moment, then three facts.
aliases: product shot that opens on scroll
called: the screenshot that tilts up as you scroll to it
product image opening like a laptop
big product shot that animates in

anatomy.name: Claim
anatomy.text: What the product is for, large and centred, with one line under it.

anatomy.name: Product
anatomy.text: The real screen in a device frame, or a photograph. Opens from 24° back and 82% size.

anatomy.name: Facts
anatomy.text: Three true figures about the product itself.

components.prompt: Build a product reveal: a centred claim (large) with one line under it, then the product (a browser frame holding the real screen, up to 1040px wide) with a soft ground shadow, then three facts as large figures with labels. The product carries a scroll-driven animation on view(): from perspective(1800px) translateY(8%) rotateX(24deg) scale(0.82) at 40% opacity to flat and full size, transform-origin at the bottom edge, over entry 10% to cover 45%, so it is open by the time it is a third of the way up the screen. Still under reduced motion and in print; in a preview box it plays once on a timer.
components.debug: Debug my product reveal. Rule out: the reveal still running when the product is in the middle of the screen (range too long); text inside the tilted frame you are meant to read while it moves; an ancestor with overflow hidden cutting the tilt; a second reveal or zoom on the page. The symptom:
components.note: For the strongest picture of the product, once per page. data-zoom="open" works on any picture; plain data-zoom only settles its size (media-band uses it).

components.name: Gallery rail
components.summary: A row of pictures at one ratio that runs off the right edge and snaps as it scrolls sideways, with previous and next buttons. Many pictures without a wall of cards.
called: a row of products you can swipe
the horizontal gallery that bleeds off the edge

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.text: Runs to the right edge of the screen so the next picture is cut: it says there is more.

anatomy.name: Buttons
anatomy.text: One picture at a time; disabled at either end.

anatomy.name: Caption
anatomy.text: The name and one fact, on one line.

components.prompt: Build a gallery rail: a heading on the left with round previous and next buttons on the right, then a row of pictures at one ratio (3:4) that starts on the page's left edge and runs off the right edge of the screen, cut mid-picture. Native horizontal scroll with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and no visible scrollbar; the track is focusable. Each picture has a one-line caption: name left, price or fact right. Buttons scroll by one picture and are disabled at either end. On phones each picture is 72% wide and the buttons hide.
components.debug: Debug my gallery rail. Rule out: a scrollbar showing; the first picture not on the page's left edge; pictures of mixed ratios; buttons that do not disable at the ends; autoplay. The symptom:
components.note: Five to twelve pictures at one ratio: a range, rooms, projects, colours. Never autoplay. For two to four things use offer-cards instead.

components.name: Side scroll
components.summary: A row of work that slides sideways while you scroll down through a tall section, pinned until the last piece arrives. On phones it is a row you swipe, with snap.
states: native swipe (phones, reduced motion, no script)
called: the section where the projects move sideways as you scroll down

anatomy.name: Heading
anatomy.text: What the row is, with one line of context beside it.

anatomy.name: Row
anatomy.text: Five to eight pictures at one ratio. Pinned, it slides by exactly its overflow; on phones it scrolls and snaps.

anatomy.name: Caption
anatomy.text: The name and one fact under each picture.

anatomy.name: Progress
anatomy.text: A short line that fills as the row travels.

components.prompt: Build a side-scroll section: a heading and one line, then a row of five to eight pictures at one ratio (4:5) with a caption each, and a short progress line. On a wide screen with motion allowed, the section is 100svh plus the row's overflow tall (a script measures the overflow into --travel with a ResizeObserver); an inner wrapper is position: sticky at the top, one screen tall, and the row is translated from 0 to -var(--travel) by the section's own view-timeline over its contain range, so it slides while the page scrolls. Tabbing to a link in a row that has slid away scrolls the page to where it is visible. On phones, under reduced motion, without script or without scroll-driven animations it is a native horizontal scroller with scroll-snap, starting on the page's left edge and running off the right. Transform only; nothing reads layout on scroll.
components.debug: Debug my side scroll. Rule out: an ancestor with overflow hidden (breaks sticky); the section height not matching the row's overflow (it ends early or dwells); a scroll listener moving the row; pinning on phones; a second pinned moment on the same page. The symptom:
code: section { view-timeline: --rail block } ul { animation: slide linear both; animation-timeline: --rail; animation-range: contain }
components.note: For work people browse: projects, a range, rooms. Five to eight pictures at one ratio. It is one of the page's two scroll moments. For a row that never pins, use gallery-rail.
